answer: An insurance-stake system makes each identity post a 40-unit stake before it can earn weight, and a random audit that finds copied work or clones forfeits the whole stake. The identity's key is struck against a ferrous plate that records a unique imprint, so one key cannot back two accounts. Each passing audit marks the stake with violet dye that fades after 30 days, and weight stops until a fresh audit renews it. After a 14-day horizon of clean audits the stake unlocks, but a failed audit burns it. 100 fakes cost 4,000 units at risk.
